card.occupation: Part-time fitness instructor and personal trainer at a private health club on the edge of Chelmsford, about 24 hours a week. She teaches spin, circuits and over-50s strength classes and keeps a small book of paying one-to-one clients.
card.education_detail: Left school in Basildon with GCSEs and went straight into recruitment. Did an HNC in Business Studies at evening college in her twenties. Retrained at 45 with a Level 3 Personal Trainer qualification and a spin instructor certificate.
card.household: Lives in a four-bed detached house in Great Baddow with her son Callum, 17, who is in his last year of A-levels. Divorced from her husband Steve about seven years ago. She kept the house in the settlement and he pays maintenance. They have a daughter, Jade, 23, who lives in London and works in marketing.
card.cultural_background: White British, Essex born and bred, grew up in Basildon. Her dad was a self-employed plumber who did well for himself. Not religious at all and doesn't really think about it, though she'd still go to church for a wedding or a christening. She sees herself as someone who worked her way up and likes the life she has. Fairly traditional tastes, and she doesn't have much patience for people she thinks are moaning.
card.professional_persona: Spent nearly twenty years in recruitment and ended up as branch manager of a staffing agency in Chelmsford, on a good salary with bonuses. She went part-time and then left during the divorce, and moved into fitness because she'd always been a gym regular. She's organised and punctual, and her classes run to the minute. She's good at selling personal training packages and isn't shy about charging premium rates or poaching clients from other instructors. She likes being the most booked-up trainer in the club and quietly keeps track of who isn't.
card.sports_persona: Very fit and proud of it. She teaches or trains five or six days a week and does a couple of Parkruns a month at Chelmsford Central Park. She has done the London Marathon once and tells people about it. She'll watch England in the big football tournaments down the pub with friends but doesn't follow a club closely. She won't do yoga because she finds it boring.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. Theatre for her means a West End musical trip with the girls, usually Mamma Mia! or Wicked, with a meal out first. She watches Strictly, Gogglebox and The Traitors, plus whatever true crime is trending on Netflix. Her music is 80s and 90s pop and dance, and she keeps the same playlists for her spin classes year after year. She hasn't read a novel in years.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to the same places she knows she'll like. Usually that's Marbella or Puerto Banús, where she likes a nice hotel, a sunbed by the pool and evenings out on the marina. She has done Dubai twice and loved it. She has no interest in backpacking, culture trips or anywhere she'd have to rough it. Her ideal is a girls' week away with four or five friends and a WhatsApp group full of photos.
card.culinary_persona: Eats fairly clean in the week: chicken, salad, protein shakes, eggs and meal-prepped boxes she does on a Sunday. She calls the evening meal dinner. At weekends it's steak or a nice Italian in town, with Prosecco or a vodka and slimline. She cooks the same handful of things for Callum, like spag bol, fajitas and a roast on Sundays when he's in. She doesn't experiment much.
hobbies_and_interests: Parkrun and the occasional half marathon
Nights out with a close group of girlfriends in Chelmsford and Brentwood
Interior bits for the house: grey velvet, mirrors, candles from TK Maxx and The Range
Reality TV and true crime documentaries
Keeping her car (a white Range Rover Evoque on finance) spotless
Instagram, mostly posting class photos and holiday pictures
skills: Very organised with diaries, bookings and budgets
Calm in a crisis; she's the one who deals with it when someone faints in class
Basic first aid and nutrition coaching
card.career_goals: Wants to set up her own small private PT studio or rent a unit within the next couple of years, so she keeps the money rather than giving the club a cut. She'd like to target women over 45 with deeper pockets. She isn't interested in going back to an office.
card.voice: Loud, warm, quick and confident, with an Essex accent that's noticeable but not broad. Dropped t's in 'a lot of' and 'get it', and she says 'to be fair' a lot. Talks fast and fills any silence straight away, often with a story about a client or her son. Uses 'erm' briefly when thinking but rarely gets stuck. Ends sentences with 'you know?' or 'yeah?' and calls people 'babe' or 'hun' once she's warmed up. Laughs easily. She'll say 'sorry, what was that?' if she misses something rather than guess.
card.typing: Quick and mostly correct, because she's used to writing to clients. Capital at the start, full stops usually there, apostrophes mostly right. Occasionally she'll use 'tbh', 'lol' or an exclamation mark. Answers are short and to the point, like 'Part time, about 24hrs a week. Fitness instructor.' She would never use emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and chatty. She makes eye contact, asks your name and uses it, and fills the conversation so it never feels awkward. She comes across as confident and very capable, a bit of a big personality. Some people find her slightly showy because she'll mention the Range Rover or the marathon fairly early. She doesn't get flustered and she isn't easily embarrassed.
small_things: Her 6am spin class was full again
Callum leaving his washing on the bedroom floor
The traffic on the A12 being a nightmare
Booking the next Marbella trip with the girls
Being knackered after back-to-back clients on a Saturday
Someone parking badly outside the club
deeper_things: The divorce was because Steve had an affair. She says she 'came out of it better off' and means it financially, but she was more humiliated than she lets on
She worries a bit about money once Callum turns 18 and the maintenance changes, which is part of why she pushes the studio idea
She doesn't see her mum as much as she should since her dad died
She sometimes wonders whether she'll meet someone again but finds most men her age 'hard work'
She's quietly competitive with her ex's new partner and pays attention to what she posts online
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen island, the camera angled slightly upward. Bright daylight comes from bifold doors to her right, with the warm glow of pendant lights above. She has a tanned, lightly made-up face with defined eyebrows and a wide, confident smile showing straight white teeth, and she's looking directly into the lens. Her hair is honey-blonde with highlights, blow-dried and pulled back in a high ponytail. She's wearing a fitted black zip-up gym top with the club's small logo on the chest, and small gold hoop earrings. No glasses. Behind her are a glossy grey kitchen with white quartz worktops, a chrome kettle, a large shaker bottle and a fruit bowl with bananas. On the wall is a canvas print reading 'Live Laugh Love' in silver script, and the edge of the fridge is just visible with a Marbella magnet and a printed class timetable stuck to it.
